previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient was admitted with fevers, rigors, and worsening cough and dyspnea following a presumed upper respiratory infection. He was found to have a retrocardial opacity on chest X-ray concerning for early pneumonia, leukocytosis, and hypotension on arrival. He received IV fluids and antibiotics in the emergency department and was admitted for further management. He improved clinically, remained afebrile, and had resolving leukocytosis by hospital day 3. His chronic conditions—including hypertension, aortic stenosis, and SIADH-related hyponatremia—were stable and managed without intervention. He was discharged home on a short course of oral levofloxacin with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider.

# SOB/cough/chest discomfort: Patient was admitted with

After discussion with his cardiologist and primary care

follow-up. He will also have an evaluation for respiratory 
therapy as an outpatient.

BP (sbp's 160's). He had not taken his morning antihypertensive 
medications and was given his evening medications on admission. 
Overnight, his blood pressure remained elevated with sbp's to 
the 170's and his morning medications were administered early to 
help control his blood pressure. They improved slightly but 
remained elevated, so he was started on Amlodipine 5mg PO daily 
in addition to his home Valsartan and Metoprolol Tartrate and 
will follow-up with his physician for ongoing management.

#. Anemia: Patient with chronic anemia and a history of negative 
iron/vitamin studies. A Hct on admission was 30.0, in keeping 
with prior Hct's. Given his history of peptic ulcer disease, he 
may have some GI blood losses, but his Hct remained stable 
throughout his stay and he did not have a bowel movement to 
guaiac during this hospitalization.

followed by Dr. ___ in ___ clinic, but patient remained without 
abdominal discomfort or distention on this admission. He 
continued his home Sucralfate and Cimetidine.

some baseline shortness of breath. This was thought to be owed

contributed to it. Otherwise, his AS was not an active issue on 
this admission.

Lidocaine patch at home. On admission, the patient noted some 
skin tears at the site of his Lidocaine patch, so his patch was 
held as an inpatient. He continued to take his Tramadol 50mg 
q6H:PRN without incident or complaints of uncontrolled pain.
